scope: Cross-check explicit MESH version/writer interoperability, peer-reported appearance fields, public DXF contracts, and downstream consumer boundaries; refine plan readiness without changing implementation or support claims.

method.kind: Primary Autodesk documentation, released peer notes/issues, consumer documentation, and local API inventory
method.evidenceBoundary: Autodesk tables define documented DXF record fields, not all native appearance semantics. Peer release summaries establish shipped change descriptions, not independent conformance. Consumer documentation is backend/version bounded. Static local API inventory does not prove runtime loss or establish a support claim.

evidence.topic: Versioned MESH writer identity is a concrete interoperability condition
observed: Autodesk's 2021 DXF MESH table identifies AcDbSubDMesh and documents version, level-0 vertices, face-list items, edges, crease values, and property-override framing/types.
ACadSharp issue #1038 describes an AC1024 DxfWriter result whose proxy metadata named MESH/AcDbSubDMesh while AutoCAD treated the entity as ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY.

The linked #1067 fix is listed in ACadSharp v3.6.12 as updating MESH version handling, DXF assertions, and edge-crease handling. This is a resolved peer failure class, not a current-release run or proof of libdxfrw behavior.
The parity plan already records Autodesk's AC1024 SUBDIVISION and AC1027 MESH spellings and the local all-version MESH writer gap.
evidence.planUse: Keep the fast local slice narrowly versioned: AC1024 SUBDIVISION, AC1027/AC1032 MESH, both readable into one DRW_Mesh. Generated ASCII/binary checks must inspect raw $ACADVER, record name, subclass, CLASS identity, crease fields, typed values, and a following sentinel. Reject proxy substitution in any optional peer result. Preserve older-target behavior until the existing source/provenance audit resolves its conflicting evidence.

evidence.topic: MESH visual-appearance parity is a newly identified classification gap, not yet a format defect
observed: ACadSharp release v3.6.35 lists merged PR #1084, described as adding material write support and MESH texture-coordinate round-trip.
Autodesk's public MESH table lists a material-mapper property-override type but does not enumerate a per-vertex UV-coordinate sequence.
Local DRW_Mesh stores topology, creases, an unknown field, and DXF propertyOverrides; the public class has no texture-coordinate member.

The release-note title alone does not identify whether the extra coordinates belong to DWG-only data, a material/mapper object, a documented DXF field omitted by the summary, or an application-specific extension.
evidence.planUse: Add a non-blocking appearance investigation before closing broad visual-fidelity claims. Pin and inspect the merged peer source/change and its exact read/write test, then classify the field route against Autodesk's public DXF contract and a source-authored control. Until that classification, label texture/material fidelity UNQUALIFIED; do not call it a proven DXF omission, add speculative fields, or mix it into MESH topology/B-rep denominators. Do not delay the ready version-name/wire-codec slice.

evidence.topic: Consumer claims must remain per importer and geometry family
observed: FreeCAD's archived Draft_DXF matrix distinguishes the C++ importer from the legacy Python importer: the cited matrix marks 3DFACE unsupported in C++ and supported in legacy, and says the importer does not read ACIS solid blobs.
FreeCAD's import/export manual describes its DXF/DWG route as 2D-only for proprietary embedded 3D data.
ezdxf's authoring documentation says creation of ACIS data requires an external library; its renderer documentation does not provide ACIS rendering or a 3D rendering engine.
evidence.planUse: Retain per-backend, per-platform FreeCAD receipts and separate explicit mesh/face acceptance from ACIS carrier and B-rep acceptance. A successful file open or converter handoff is not geometry acceptance; use object type/topology and independent analytic properties when the named consumer supports that family.

nextActions: Implement the already-ready version-to-record-name choice and parser alias using the existing generated DXF fixture target; preserve older-target behavior pending its existing witness audit.
At the next optional peer checkpoint, pin ACadSharp release/source and require native MESH identity, version, topology, crease values, appearance fields, and diagnostics to be reported separately.
Classify ACadSharp's MESH texture/material route before deciding whether it is standard DXF, DWG-only, or extension data; add no speculative model fields before that evidence.
Keep FreeCAD results bound to importer backend/platform and distinguish explicit mesh/face shape construction from ACIS/B-rep support.
